newsitem.title: JAPAN: Drug haul from North Korea ship in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Drug haul from North Korea ship in Japan.

text.p: Police in southern Japan said on Friday that they had found a large cache of illegal drugs in cargo from a North Korean freighter and arrested two ethnic Koreans.

A police spokesman in Miyazaki on Japan's southern island of Kyushu refused to disclose the exact size of the cache, but Japanese media said it was a 70 kg (154 lb) haul of amphetamines -- with a street value estimated at 11.9 billion yen ($95 million).
The spokesman said police found a "large amount" of amphetamines in cargo labelled as honey at the port of Hososhima on the Pacific coast of Kyushu island.
He said two Korean residents of Japan had been arrested.
The ship was the 1,499-tonne North Korean freighter Ji Song-2 which left the North Korean port of Nanpo on April 5 for the Japanese port, the police spokesman said.
Investigators were questioning the two ethnic Koreans arrested as well as the captain and 17 crew members, he said.

Earlier on Friday, Foreign Ministry spokesman Ken Shimanouchi denied knowledge of the arrests and drug seizure, but said Japan was wary of extending aid to North Korea, which is currently gripped by a severe food shortage.
Japan's already chilly ties with North Korea worsened recently after a North Korean defector said Northern agents kidnapped a Japanese schoolgirl who had disappeared in 1977.
"We have to take into account...how Japanese feel about extending assistance to North Korea," Shimanouchi told a news conference.

"Japanese people are not necessarily comfortable with the idea of extending assistance to North Korea when such issues as the suspected kidnappings of Japanese and the issue of Japanese wives in North Korea remain unresolved," he said. ($1=125 yen)
